“Go put on a uniform and have a gun pulled on you. We’ll see how long you last”

I never understood the, "you go be a cop" argument either. Becoming a cop is a decision they make (not me) and they should know the risks involved, such as being shot.

The argument isn't knowing about the risks, it's about living with the risks. It's superficial saying you know what a cop goes through just because you read about the risks, few have ever been in a situation where the risk is real. It's the difference between seeing a bear in the zoo and seeing a bear in the wild. That's the argument.

The response argument being they chose it. The civilian deaths overseas that our troops are responsible for, are they any less at fault for those deaths because of the line of duty they chose is so dangerous? I think not, I think that's an excuse used to make it seem as if police have it so hard we should simply expect a civilian or 2 to catch a bullet here or there. The fault in that logic? It doesn't occur in any other modern country with police but ours...

I'm not defending police officers, I'm just saying that the response to

“Go put on a uniform and have a gun pulled on you. We’ll see how long you last”

being

"You chose this, it's what you wanted. You knew the risks"

isn't a great argument in my eyes. Cops are people too, some are just as scared as anyone else. Obviously, I'm not saying that's okay that certain police officers can injure, maim, or kill a few civilians and face no repercussions. What I'm saying is that being put in some dangerous situations and expected to react, not as a civilian but an enforcer, a lot of things can go wrong. What ever happens in that situation the officer to be held responsible, but do not expect that in every situation it will go by the books. People are flawed, they react unexpectedly, and they are selfish. Officer's want to go home and pay the bills, they want to do their job as fast as possible to minimize any prolonged threat to themselves and they're probably angry that they have to deal with another guy on a long shift. If we want officers to do everything by the books, we should just get robots; their behavior and actions is pre-programmed, their actions are be predictable and they won't worry about their own safety.

Police brutality is inexcusable, but we aren't dealing with model police officers, we're dealing with people in uniforms. They're held too high in regards and it should be seen to changing how they operate with civilians and among themselves. Too many police officers are holding their "brotherhood" too high and they feel they can get away with it, leading to cops believing they can behave outside of procedure with less repercussions and some take it too far. Once again, people are selfish.
